resources.string: Lets ReelyRelay notice when you select a movie or show recommendation on your TV\'s home screen, so it can offer to open it in Reely Player.

When you pick a movie or show on your TV\'s home screen, ReelyRelay offers to open it in Reely Player instead of the app it came from.\n\nTo do that it uses an Accessibility Service - only on the home screen, and only to read the title of the recommendation you select. That title is sent to TMDB to identify it. Nothing else is read, stored or sent, and every other click is left alone.
This is what lets ReelyRelay see which recommendation you pick. Open Accessibility, choose ReelyRelay and switch it on, then press Back to return here.
Find ReelyRelay in the list and switch it on
Fire TV\'s home screen doesn\'t tell apps which recommendation you picked, so ReelyRelay reads the title off the screen instead. That takes two permissions, both set up on the next screen.
Recommended. Before anything opens, ReelyRelay shows a button to confirm, so a stray click never sends you to Reely Player by accident. Without it, titles open straight away.

About reading titles from the screen

Some recommendations - especially the \"Top picks for you\" row - don\'t include a readable title in the click ReelyRelay receives. With this on, ReelyRelay uses Android\'s screen-recording permission to read the title off the screen, on the device. Nothing captured leaves it.\n\nAndroid shows its recording indicator the whole time this is on. ReelyRelay can\'t hide it.
Only to identify a title it couldn\'t detect any other way.
On - turn it on again after a restart

ReelyRelay notices when you open a recommendation and reads its title off the screen, on the device. It needs two permissions: Usage access, to notice the recommendation, and Screen recording, to read the title.\n\nAndroid shows its recording indicator while this is on. The screen-recording permission is cleared by a restart, so turn Fire TV mode on again after one.

Android blocks Accessibility for apps installed by hand. It\'s a safeguard, not a bug. If \"Allow restricted setting\" isn\'t in the app info screen, run this over ADB (the atvTools app can do it from a phone):
adb shell appops set %1$s ACCESS_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS allow
Scan the code for the full walkthrough.
Look for \"Allow restricted setting\" - not on every device
